prs.title: Add positional HTML insertion methods
prs.author: noamr
prs.body:
Add `appendHTML()`, `prependHTML()`, `beforeHTML()`, `afterHTML()`, and `replaceWithHTML()`, alongside their `*Unsafe()` variants.

`NonDocumentTypeChildNode` methods fail silently when the child has no parent, like their equivalent DOM methods, and fail with a `"HierarchyRequestError"` `DOMException` for an invalid parent (`Document`, hostless `DocumentFragment`, `template` element, or `html` element). `appendHTML()` and `prependHTML()` (and their `*Unsafe()` variants) also throw a `"HierarchyRequestError"` `DOMException` when called on an `html` element, as parsing a fragment with an `html` context element always produces both a `head` and a `body` element.

Note that the new `NonDocumentTypeChildNode` methods are also exposed on `CharacterData`.

Renamed "set and filter HTML" to "filter and set HTML" to be more consistent with the order of operations and with the newly added helper methods.

Closes #10122

- [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed):
   * Chrome
   * Gecko (https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/1370)
- [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at:
   * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/60555
- [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed:
   * Chromium: Implemented
   * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=315741
   * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.

prs.title: Sanitize while parsing
prs.author: noamr
prs.body:
Sanitize while parsing, instead of parsing into a fragment and then walking it.

The sanitizer configuration is passed into the HTML parser, which consults it wherever it would create or insert a node: disallowed elements are never created or inserted (or are replaced by their children, by redirecting insertions to where the element would have gone), disallowed attributes are dropped before the element is created, and disallowed comments and processing instructions are discarded. The separate post-parse "sanitize" algorithm is gone; the safe variants are expressed by applying their restrictions to the configuration up front.

Consequences of doing this in the parser:

- No custom element constructors run for elements the sanitizer discards (they get no definition and a null registry), and no speculative fetches are started while sanitizing.
- When sanitizing, fragment parsing builds its result in the inert document and adopts it into the target afterwards, so discarded elements never exist in the target document (#12560).
- Declarative shadow roots are only attached when `<template>` and `shadowrootmode` survive the configuration; `<template for>` patching as well.
- Insertion locations are computed after element creation, since creating a customized built-in can run script.
